To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the glass vial surface is highly heterogenous in terms of chemical composition, topography and surface energy and that the surface quality of glass vials can be improved by appropriate pre‐treatments.
the glass vial surface is heterogeneous and that the vial‐to ‐vial variations within a vial lot are larger than the variations along the vial circumference.
the inner surface of the vials is heterogeneous in nature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of a novel type of glass vials for lyophilized drug products.
the development of a method for characterization of the surface properties of glass primary packaging material for the purpose of selecting an appropriate glass vial.
the development and application of analytical methods to characterize the surface properties and glass surface interactions with parenteral products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all vials investigated showed heterogeneity and/or variability in surface properties.
the surface of a glass vial is heterogeneous and varies between different vial types, within one vial type as well as between different vials of the same lot.
the glass vials studied are not equivalent and should be treated differently during the manufacturing process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glass surface of the vials is very complex and the composition of the surface varies significantly from lot-to-lot, vial-to-vial and even within a single vial.
a glass vial is not just a glass vial, and the selection of an adequate vial is not solely dependent on the hydrolytic class of the glass.
the surface of glass vials is highly variable and heterogeneous, and this is especially true when no surface treatment is performed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glass vial surface is not homogenous and that the glass vials should be characterized in detail prior to use.
the glass vial surface is not homogeneous and that the inner vial wall surface properties can vary significantly from one lot to the other.
the surface properties of the glass vial are of high importance for the quality of the parenteral drug product, and the selection of the glass vials should be based on the desired product quality.
